subject.title: Add confirmation step to /new and /reset to prevent accidental session wipes

question: Should manual `/new` and hard `/reset` require a default-on confirmation across all user-facing command surfaces, and should there be any config opt-out?
rationale: The code change is straightforward in several places, but the durable behavior changes public command semantics, channel UX, and possibly configuration defaults.

options.title: Default-on single confirmation
options.body: Require one repeated command or explicit confirm action before destructive manual resets, with no new config unless a concrete opt-out need is approved.

options.title: Configurable confirmation
options.body: Add a documented config/default surface for confirmation behavior, accepting the extra schema, docs, and migration review burden.

options.title: Keep command behavior unchanged
options.body: Leave typed `/new` and `/reset` immediate and rely on non-destructive session creation or recovery improvements elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Default-on single confirmation
recommendation.body: Require one repeated command or explicit confirm action before destructive manual resets, with no new config unless a concrete opt-out need is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the clearest recent history across the current reset command paths and prior UI confirmation guard.
